prompt: From forty kilometres up at night, looking west down the whole length of Britain's south-west peninsula, Devon and Cornwall narrowing into the black Atlantic: a thin chain of small amber towns along both coasts, Plymouth the brightest cluster on its harbour. Across the peninsula, a scattering of tiny orange pinpoint flashes the size of sparks, each trailing a hair of smoke, and several towns already gone dark. The sea pure black, a thin pale line of atmosphere on the horizon. Long lens, a real photograph taken from altitude, quiet and grainy. 16:9, no labels or text.
